TOKYO, Oct 7 : The Bank of Japan's new policymaker Ayano Sato said she supports the idea of raising interest rates in several stages, Kyodo news agency reported on Wednesday, highlighting awareness even among dovish board members of the need to combat inflation risks. Appointed by Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, who favours looser monetary policy, Sato was one of two dissenters to the BOJ's decision to raise interest rates in September. She joined the nine-member board in June. In the interview with Kyodo, Sato said she decided to vote against last month's rate hike because consumption lacked momentum and underlying inflation was not picking up pace. "I support the idea that interest rates should be adjusted in stages, as current financial conditions are accommodative," Sato was quoted as saying, adding that the appropriate timing of future rate hikes would depend on developments in consumption and income.

Sato also said there should not be any pre-set pace for future rate hikes, according to Kyodo. Risks to the price outlook were "somewhat skewed to the upside" due to rising crude oil prices linked to the Middle East conflict, Sato said. INFLATION APPROACHING 2 per cent Along with Toichiro Asada, another newcomer appointed by Takaichi, Sato has been seen by markets as among doves on the nine-member board who could continue to vote against rate hikes. Their dissents in September pushed down the yen as market players interpreted the move as a sign the BOJ's rate-hike plans would continue to face opposition from Takaichi's administration. Sato told Kyodo that BOJ rate hikes could contribute to achieving sustained economic growth. The central bank would set policy independently, but in a way that "eventually aligns with the administration's proactive fiscal policy," she said. After spending years treading cautiously in policy normalisation, the BOJ picked up pace in raising rates by hiking in June and September as the Iran war-induced energy shock added to price pressures from rising import costs via a weak yen. Upon hiking rates to a 31-year high of 1.25 per cent in September, Governor Kazuo Ueda said the central bank had entered a phase focused on preventing underlying inflation from overshooting its target, raising the prospect of tighter policy. While the BOJ may pause in October, it is likely to drop hawkish hints that would reinforce dominant market expectations of a December hike, sources have told Reuters. In a separate interview with the daily Asahi newspaper, Sato said underlying inflation was approaching the BOJ's 2 per cent target, adding that her views on monetary policy were "not that different from many others in the board."

Source: Reuters

item.content:encoded:
マーベル、28年度売上高200億ドル見込む　ＡＩ向けカスタム半導体がけん引 7:03 配信

１0月６日、米ニューヨークで開催されたマーベル・テクノロジーの投資家向け説明会。 REUTERS/Eduardo Munoz

Prathik Jayaprakash　Anhata Rooprai　Max A. Cherney

[６日 ロイター] - 米半導体大手マーベル・テクノロジー が６日発表した２０２８会計年度の売上高見通しは約２００億ドルと、ＬＳＥＧがまとめた市場予想の１８２億ドルを上回った。人工知能（ＡＩ）関連投資の拡大を背景に、データセンター向けカスタム半導体の需要が伸びると見込む。

クリス・クープマンズ社長兼最高執行責任者（ＣＯＯ）はインタビューで「会社をこの軌道に乗せ、技術面でリーダーになるまでには長い時間がかかった。われわれには約束したことを実行してきた実績がある」と語った。

マーベルは２１年、データセンター向けに特化して設計するカスタム半導体やクラウド最適化半導体を軸とする戦略を打ち出した。その後ＡＩインフラ投資拡大の恩恵を受けており、２９会計年度のカスタム半導体事業の売上高について、従来の１００億ドルから１２０億ドルに目標を引き上げた。

大手テクノロジー企業がエヌビディア 製半導体への依存を減らすためにＡＩ向け半導体の自社開発を進める中、マーベルのカスタム半導体事業は主要な成長の柱となっている。それに伴って同社の株価は今年に入って３倍超に上昇した。

さらに中長期目標としてマーベルが示した３１会計年度売上高見通しは７００億－９００億ドルだった。レンジの中央値となる８００億ドルは、ビジブル・アルファがまとめたアナリスト４人の市場予想４６８億５０００万ドルを大幅に上回っている。

item.description: ＜為替＞ ニューヨーク外為市場ではユーロが上昇し、１日としては７週間ぶりの大幅な上昇を記録する見通し。フランス国債利回り...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ＮＹ市場サマリー（6日）Ｓ＆Ｐ５００とナスダックが最高値更新、ユーロ上昇、利回り低下 7:00 配信

9月29日、ニューヨーク証券取引所。 REUTERS/Jeenah Moon

＜為替＞ ニューヨーク外為市場ではユーロが上昇し、１日としては７週間ぶりの大幅な上昇を記録する見通し。フランス国債利回りの低下を受け、ユーロ圏債市場の緊張に対する懸念が和らいだ。

ユーロ／ドルは０．３５％高の１．１２６ドル。１日としては８月１９日以来の大幅高となる見通し。前日の取引では、約１年５カ月ぶりの安値を付ける場面もあった。

主要通貨に対するドル指数は０．３２％安の１０１．８３。１日の下げとしては９月３日以来最大となる見込み。

原油相場の落ち着きを背景に、仏１０年債利回りは６日の取引で低下。同債利回りはここ数週間で急上昇し、指標となる独債との利回り格差は月初に２０１１年のユーロ圏債務危機以来の最大水準に拡大していた。

ポンド／ドルは１週間ぶりの高値となる１．３２８３ドルを付けた後、終盤の取引では０．４２％高の１．３２７５ドル。ポンドも１日としては８月１９日以来の大幅高となる勢い。

ＮＹ外為市場：[USD/J]

＜債券＞ 米金融・債券市場では国債利回りが低下した。前日の取引で国債が売り込まれた反動で買戻しが入った。３年債入札が堅調だったことも利回り低下に寄与した。市場では米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）の金融政策の行方を見極めようと、来週発表されるインフレ指標が注目されている。

前日の取引では、高金利環境の長期化見通しが織り込まれたことで１０年債と３０年債の利回りが約２４年ぶりの水準に上昇。ＦＨＮフィナンシャル（シカゴ）のマクロストラテジスト、ウィル・コンパーノール氏は、この日は「ファンダメンタルズ（基礎的要件）が変化する前に一服する動きが出た」と指摘。「市場では次の大きな材料を見極める動きが出ている」とし、「次の材料が卸売物価指数（ＰＰＩ）になるのか、消費者物価指数（ＣＰＩ）になるのかは分からないが、利回りはすでに高水準にあり、さらに上昇するにはその動きを正当化するより説得力のある材料が必要になる」と述べた。

市場関係者によると、この日はユーロ圏の国債利回りが低下したことも米国債利回りの低下に寄与した。特に、懸念の的になっていたフランス国債利回りが低下したことが米国債市場にも波及したとしている。

終盤の取引で１０年債利回りは前日比４．２ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）低下の５．２６９％。３０年債利回りは２．２ｂｐ低下の５．６４２％。

２年債利回りは４．４ｂｐ低下の４．７８９％。

米金融・債券市場：[US/BJ]

＜株式＞ 米国株式市場は続伸。幅広い銘柄が買われ、Ｓ＆Ｐ総合５００種とナスダック総合が最高値を更新して引けた。原油価格が落ち着き、米国債利回りも低下したことで、ここ数週間に投資家を悩ませてきた懸念が和らぎ、市場の関心は間近に迫った第３・四半期決算発表シーズンに向かった。

ダウ工業株３０種は８月５日に付けた終値での最高値を５％余り下回っている。

ウェルスパイア・アドバイザーズのシニアバイスプレジデント、オリバー・パーシェ氏は、原油価格が安定または下落すると「エネルギー価格高騰によるインフレへの不安が和らぐため利回りが低下し、それが株価の上昇を後押しする」と指摘。「ここ数週間の市場はこうした構図で動いてきた」と述べた。

超大型株「マグニフィセント・セブン」のうち６銘柄が上昇し、相場を押し上げた。一方、小型株指数のラッセル２０００はアンダーパフォームした。

人工知能（ＡＩ）関連株への買いは依然として健在で、フィラデルフィア半導体株指数（ＳＯＸ指数）も上昇した。ＡＩ関連インフラへの支出は貿易統計にも表れ、８月の資本財輸入は４．４％増加した。

米国株式市場：[.NJP]

＜金先物＞ 米長期金利の上昇一服やドル安を背景に、金相場は上昇した。投資家は米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）の９月会合議事要旨の公表を注視している。

中心限月１２月物の清算値は前日比０．７％高の１オンス＝４１８７．１０ドル。１８１２ＧＭＴ（日本時間７日午前３時１２分）現在、現物価格は０．７％高の１オンス＝４１６８．３３ドル。

米１０年債利回りは前日に２０年以上ぶりの高水準まで上昇した後、やや低下。ドルも１年ぶり高値から下落し、他通貨保有者にとって金が割安となった。

ＮＹ貴金属：[GOL/XJ]

＜米原油先物＞ 米国時間の原油先物は序盤の下げを取り戻し、ほぼ横ばいで終了した。中東からの原油輸出の増加や主要７カ国（Ｇ７）による緊急備蓄からのディーゼル燃料放出計画と、イエメンの親イラン武装組織フーシ派の攻撃に伴う供給懸念とを見極める展開となった。

清算値は、北海ブレント先物が０．２６ドル（０．３％）高の１バレル＝１００．５８ドル。米ＷＴＩ先物は０．０１ドル高の８９．４４ドル。

大手石油商社ビトルの最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は６日、価格上昇圧力を和らげるために必要な量とされる日量約１２００万バレルの原油と同２００万バレルの石油製品が、過去７─１０日間に中東から出荷されたと明らかにした。

サウジアラビアのアブドルアジズエネルギー相も６日、紅海沿岸の石油輸出拠点ヤンブーに通じる東西パイプラインの送油量が、同日朝の時点で５８０万バレルに達したと明らかにした。

こうした中、サウジアラビア航空当局は、フーシ派との対立が激化する中、ジャザンとナジュランにあるサウジの２空港が５日に攻撃の標的となり、３人が負傷し、限定的な被害が出たと明らかにした。中東でのさらなる供給途絶の可能性が意識され、原油価格の下落幅は限定的なものにとどまった。

ＮＹＭＥＸエネルギー：[CR/USJ]

item.title: North Korea criticises US support for Taiwan, pledges backing for Russia
item.description: North Korea criticised the United States over its arms sales and military support for Taiwan, accusing Washington of fuelling tension in the Taiwan Strait, state news agency KCNA said on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Joyce Lee
item.content:encoded: North Korea criticised the United States over its arms sales and military support for Taiwan, accusing Washington of fuelling tension in the Taiwan Strait, state news agency KCNA said on Wednesday. A KCNA commentary citing North Korean international affairs analyst Kim Myong Chol said US policy on Taiwan was undermining peace and stability in the region and condemned the appearance of US-sold fighter aircraft in Taiwan. The US "should think twice whether it is ready to stand in frontal confrontation with the powerful national power of the People's Republic of China for the security of Taiwan and whether it can cope with its consequences," it added. [USN:L1N45O07H TEXT:"Last week"], Taiwan received the first two of a batch of 66 new F-16V Block 70 fighter jets ordered in 2019, in the face of a rising military threat from Beijing. The comments show Pyongyang is aligning more closely with China on Taiwan, one of Beijing's most sensitive foreign policy issues. China claims the democratically governed island as its own, though Taipei rejects the sovereignty assertion. North Korea has strengthened ties with China and Russia in recent years, raising security concerns for the US and its allies in Asia and the West. KIM OFFERED FULL SUPPORT AT JUNE SUMMIT North Korean leader Kim Jong Un told Chinese President Xi Jinping during a Pyongyang summit in June that he would [USN:L1N42G106 TEXT:"fully support"] the "One China" principle, which Beijing views as meaning that both sides of the Taiwan Strait belong to one country, regardless of changes in the international situation. The meeting also included a cautiously worded reference to defence links, with Xi saying both sides would enhance exchanges in diplomacy, law enforcement, military affairs and other fields, China's Foreign Ministry said. Analysts have said North Korea's decision to send soldiers to fight for Russia in the Ukraine war had shown it is willing to provide material assistance in wartime, but with no sign of a comparable commitment to China. China describes Taiwan as the "core of core issues" in its ties with other countries, demanding no form of official engagement between Taiwanese and foreign leaders. Taiwan's government says Beijing has no right to claim the island or try to represent it on the international stage. China, a treaty ally of North Korea, has also repeatedly demanded that Washington end arms sales to Taiwan. The United States is bound by law to provide Taiwan with the means to defend itself, despite the lack of formal diplomatic ties. Kim pledged continued support for Russia and its war effort in a birthday message to President Vladimir Putin, KCNA said in a separate report. Pyongyang would keep up joint work under their comprehensive strategic partnership, Kim said. He was convinced that Russia's "sacred war of justice" to defend its sovereignty, security interests and territorial integrity would end in victory, he added. The message did not explicitly mention Russia's war in Ukraine. North Korea has sent an estimated 14,000 to 15,000 troops to [USN:L1N45K11J TEXT:"support Russia"] in the conflict since 2024, according to Ukrainian and South Korean estimates. North Korea and Russia have strengthened ties sharply since a mutual defence pact signed in June 2024.

item.description: In Asia, MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares excluding Japan was down 0.3% after US stocks ended higher. The index is up 1.5% so far this month ...
item.content:encoded:
Home / Markets / News / Asian shares weaker as investors weigh Saudi Arabia-Houthi escalation

Asian shares weaker as investors weigh Saudi Arabia-Houthi escalation In Asia, MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares excluding Japan was down 0.3% after US stocks ended higher. The index is up 1.5% so far this month

Image: Bloomberg

Reuters SYDNEY 4 min read Last Updated : Oct 07 2026 | 10:10 AM IST

Listen to This Article

Asian markets were slightly weaker on Wednesday even though US stocks touched new highs, as oil prices rose with a storm heading for the Gulf of Mexico and tensions escalating between Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis. In Asia, MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares excluding Japan was down 0.3% after US stocks ended higher. The index is up 1.5% so far this month. The S&P 500 hit a fresh record on Tuesday, up about 0.6% on the day, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq gained 0.45%, also an all-time high. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.5%. In Asian trading, US crude ticked up 1.05% to $90.38 a barrel; prices were little changed in the international session. Brent crude rose 1.06% to $101.65 per barrel.

The price rise came as commodity investors weighed supply constraints from a storm heading for North American oil-producing regions and Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia against increased supplies of Middle East crude. Also Read

Asian shares track Wall Street higher, Treasury yields near decades high

Stocks to watch: Trent, Vedanta, Axis Bank, Adani Power, Marico & more

Asian shares tumble after wild swings in bonds, FX before US jobs data

Asian shares mostly rise as tech stocks gain despite Iran war worries

Mkt crash wipes off ₹7.4 trn; Sensex down 1,180 pts intraday: 5 key factors

Around 12 million barrels per day (bpd) of crude oil and 2 million bpd of refined products have left the Middle East on tankers in the last 7 to 10 days, commodities trading giant Vitol's CEO Russell Hardy said on Tuesday. The positive sentiment among traders of US equities followed a stabilisation in global bond yields overnight. Heavily sold French debt pulled back on Tuesday as far-right presidential candidate Marine Le Pen pledged spending cuts and a reduction in the country's budget deficit. Ten-year French yields fell more than 11 basis points and the spread between French OATs and German bunds, which hit almost 160 bps last week, according to LSEG data, narrowed to 132 bps.

"The magnitude of the move is striking given the 2027 election remains several months away and France's deteriorating fiscal dynamics are hardly new," said Laura Cooper, Nuveen's head of macro credit and global investment strategist. "What has changed is sharply higher yields, leaving investors less willing to look through those vulnerabilities." That decline helped the euro make a small recovery and stabilise just above $1.1250. "A sense of calm returned to European bond markets with French, Italian and Greek bonds outperforming amid a broad rally," ANZ economists wrote in a note. Ten-year US Treasuries rose back to 5.3% in Asian morning trade. Longer-term US yields were edging higher on Wednesday ahead of a 10-year auction later in the session and a 30-year auction on Thursday. The auctions will show the depth of investor demand for US debt, analysts said. US longer-dated yields hit a 24-year high on Monday amid a persistent selloff since late August due to inflation and debt concerns.

Australian shares were flat on Wednesday, while Japan's Nikkei stock index was off 0.86%. Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index was down 0.63% in early trading, dragged lower by a 4% decline in the index's biotech index. Mainland China's financial markets remained closed for a holiday. The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies, rose 0.03% to 101.94 following a 0.27% slide in the prior session. The Japanese yen weakened 0.19% to 158.43 per dollar. Sterling dipped 0.08% to $1.3262. A stabilisation in oil prices in the US trading session, the euro's slight recovery and US Treasury bond yield shifts put pressure on the dollar, CBA analysts said.

The Federal Reserve on Wednesday will publish the minutes of its September 15 and 16 policy meeting, which will be scrutinised for potential rate moves over the next few months. Traders scaled back expectations of a Fed rate increase this month to 19% from about 50% a week earlier. Spot gold was recently higher at $4165.53 per ounce.

(Only the headline and picture of this report may have been reworked by the Business Standard staff; the rest of the content is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)

FAST

Oct 6 : Credit-scoring giant Fair Isaac, known as FICO, said on Tuesday it would trim about 15 per cent of its workforce as part of a broader restructuring and AI integration, becoming the latest US company to cut jobs as businesses automate tasks and redirect spending toward the technology. "This simplified structure will allow us to operate and bring innovations to market faster and create more value for our customers," FICO told Reuters in a statement. It did not specify the number of employees laid off. Fair Isaac had 3,811 employees at the end of September 2025, meaning the cuts could affect about 570 workers. It began notifying employees this week. It said it expects about $27 million in pre-tax charges in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, primarily related to severance. The plan is largely expected to be completed by the third quarter of fiscal 2027.

REGULATORY PUSH WEIGHS ON SHARES Shares of the company — known for its FICO score, a measure of consumer credit risk widely used by banks, credit card issuers, mortgage lenders and auto loan providers — have plunged about 58 per cent this year as US regulators seek to loosen its longstanding hold on mortgage credit scoring. Last month, the US Federal Housing Finance Agency (FHFA) directed mortgage finance giants Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac to allow all lenders to use VantageScore, a rival developed by Equifax, Experian and TransUnion, for credit scoring. FHFA director Bill Pulte also said Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac would adopt a single pricing grid for both VantageScore and FICO scores, effectively putting the rivals on equal footing and threatening FICO's dominance as the standard measure of consumer credit risk in mortgage lending.

FAST

Oct 6 : Black Hills Corp said on Tuesday it signed agreements to power a proposed Google data center in Cheyenne, Wyoming, and plans to spend $1.8 billion from 2027 to 2029 on new generation capacity, as tech firms race to secure electricity for power-hungry AI data centers. • Black Hills said it will build 564 megawatts (MW) of new generation capacity for the Cheyenne project • The project is expected to draw on a 2.7-gigawatt (GW) resource mix, including reserve margins, with power deliveries set to begin in late 2027 and peak load expected in 2030 • Black Hills will supply up to 590 MW from the grid, mostly from a new gas plant at its Cheyenne Prairie Generating Station and manage about 2.1 GW of third-party resources in Wyoming through a privately managed microgrid

item.description: [６日 ロイター] - 米人工知能（ＡＩ）開発企業アンソロピックは、審査を受けたサイバーセキュリティー専門家が、同社の...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米アンソロピック、強力なＡＩモデルの開放拡大　セキュリティーチーム対象 6:07 配信

米アンソロピックのロゴ。6月撮影。REUTERS/Dado Ruvic

[６日　ロイター] - 米人工知能（ＡＩ）開発企業アンソロピックは、審査を受けたサイバーセキュリティー専門家が、同社の最も強力なＡＩモデルを安全対策を緩和した状態でテストできるプログラムを拡大する。同社のサイバーセキュリティー対策の取り組み「プロジェクト・グラスウィング」が今年、１０万件を超えるソフトウエアの脆弱（ぜいじゃく）性を発見するのに貢献したことを受けた動き。

同社が発表した新たな「サイバー検証プログラム（ＣＶＰ）」は、同社が過去６カ月間にわたり運営してきた「グラスウィング」と従来のＣＶＰの２つのプログラムを統合したものとなる。

新たなプログラムは３つの階層で構成され、それぞれ独自の検証要件とセキュリティー管理措置が設けられる。いずれの階層も「クロード・オーパス５．５」「ソネット５．５」「ミュトス５．１」、および今後のモデルへのアクセスが含まれる。

「ディフェンス」層は、インシデント対応やマルウエア解析などの業務を対象とする。企業内のセキュリティーチーム、重要インフラ事業者、オープンソースのメンテナー、脆弱性の報告実績のある研究者が申請できる。

「レッドチーム」層では、承認された侵入テストやレッドチーム活動が追加されるが、申請できるのは組織に限られる。

「スペシャライズド」層は制限が最も少なく、電力網や航空運航システム、銀行間送金インフラといった、安全性が極めて重要なシステムのテストを許可された少数の組織に限定される。アンソロピックは米政府と共同で各メンバーの審査を行い、既存のグラスウィング参加組織はこの階層に移行することになる。

item.title: ＦＲＢ、銀行監督機能再編へ 説明責任強化＝ボウマン副議長
item.description:
Pete Schroeder
[ワシントン ６日 ロイター] - 米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）のボウマン副議長（金融監督...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ＦＲＢ、銀行監督機能再編へ　説明責任強化＝ボウマン副議長 6:02 配信

２０１２年３月撮影　REUTERS/Joshua Roberts

Pete Schroeder

[ワシントン　６日　ロイター] - 米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）のボウマン副議長（金融監督担当）は６日、ＦＲＢは銀行の監督体制を抜本的に見直し、説明責任を強化する新たなモデルに移行すると明らかにした。

ボウマン氏によると、新たな体制下では全米を５つの地域に再編し、それぞれに「地域責任者（リージョナルリーダー）」を配置する。地域責任者の選考は来年初めにも開始されるという。

現在はワシントンのＦＲＢ当局者が銀行検査の方針を策定し、実際の監督業務は全米１２地区の連銀が実施。ボウマン氏はセントルイス地区連銀での講演で、現行の体制は「責任と説明責任を結び付ける重要な仕組みが機能しにくくなっている」とし、「説明責任と明確な意思決定権限を実現するためＦＲＢの監督機能を再編する」と述べた。

新体制の下では、新設される地域責任者が各地域の監督業務全般を統括するが、実際の監督業務は引き続き各地区連銀の職員が担当する。

ボウマン氏はまた、ＦＲＢが銀行監督業務を行う際に各委員会に過度に依存していることに苦言を呈し、こうした委員会の存在が銀行で問題が発生した際の対応の遅れや、ＦＲＢ職員の責任の所在の不明確化につながっていると指摘。運営を効率化する必要があるとの考えを示した。

このほか、ＦＲＢは銀行規制に適用される資産基準の見直しを年内に検討すると表明。ロイターは９月、ＦＲＢがこうした計画を進めていると報じていた。実現すれば、銀行は資本規制や流動性規制、ストレステスト（健全性審査）などが適用される前に、より大きな規模に成長できるようになる可能性がある。

ボウマン氏によると、この取り組みの一環としてＦＲＢは固定されている資産額の基準を見直すほか、物価情勢や経済成長を反映するために５年ごとに基準額を自動的に更新する仕組みの導入を検討する。

item.title: U.S. stocks rise to a record on expectations companies will make even fatter profits
item.description: Asian shares were mostly higher on Tuesday and U.S. futures advanced after shares rose to near a record close on Wall Street.
item.dc:creator: The Associated Press
item.content:encoded: NEW YORK — The U.S. stock market has never been higher, even though the list of challenges chipping away at it keeps growing. The S&P 500 climbed 0.6 per cent Tuesday to a record after topping its prior all-time high set in August. Despite worries about everything from war to high inflation to pressure from the bond market, the index at the heart of many 401(k) accounts has soared 23 per cent since hitting a bottom in late March. The Dow Jones Industrial Average added 253 points, or 0.5 per cent, while the Nasdaq composite tacked 0.4 per cent onto its own all-time high set the day before. The record-high stock prices are helping investors feel better about their finances, or at least less bad, when Americans are generally feeling discouraged about keeping up with the fast-rising cost of living. Many of the fears that sent the U.S. stock market to its bottom in March have indeed come true. Oil prices are high because of the war with Iran, which has made inflation worse. Yields have cranked higher in the bond market, which threatens to slow the economy by making it more expensive for everyone to borrow money. And Americans broadly say they’re feeling more pessimistic about the economy and where it’s heading. But one vital source of support has remained resolute for the U.S. stock market throughout: the relentless ability for companies to make more money. Lamb Weston, which sells frozen fries and other potato products, said on Tuesday that its profit and revenue during its latest quarter topped its projections, for example. The results also beat analysts’ expectations, and its stock rallied 7.5 per cent. CEO Mike Smith said the company continues to deal with unexpected increases in freight and other expenses. But the company nevertheless raised its forecast for an underlying measure of profit for its full fiscal year. It’s not just potato products proving to be profitable. All kinds of companies are lining up to report soon how much profit they made from July through September, and expectations are high. Delta Air Lines will report its third-quarter results on Friday, with several of the country’s biggest banks headlining the following week. Analysts expect companies in the S&P 500 to deliver overall growth of nearly 30 per cent in earnings per share from a year earlier, according to FactSet. If they’re correct, it would be the third straight quarter of growth better than 25 per cent. That’s crucial because corporate profits are one of the main levers that set prices for stocks, along with interest rates. At the moment, high bond yields are making investors less willing to pay high prices for investments that aren’t bonds. But the simultaneous strength for corporate profits is allowing the market to stay high and “to win the tug-of-war against yields,” according to strategists at Barclays. To be sure, much hinges on companies actually meeting those expectations for fatter profits. If they fail to do so, stock prices could easily fall off their records. Some critics also point to a possible bubble in stocks in the artificial-intelligence industry after how much they soared in the frenzy around the technology. AI stocks have been a huge force driving the U.S. market to records, including Nvidia’s 28.3 per cent surge so far this year. That’s roughly double the broad market’s gain. Constellation Energy jumped 12.2 per cent for one of Tuesday’s biggest gains in the S&P 500 because it’s also riding that rising tide. It announced a long-term deal to supply Google with about as much electricity as a new nuclear reactor makes. The boom in AI data centers has made not just electricity more in demand but also construction crews and materials throughout the economy. Elsewhere on Wall Street, Option Care Health soared 32.6 per cent after CD&R and McKesson said they’re buying the provider of infusion services. The two are paying US$32.05 for each Option Care Health share, valuing it at roughly US$5.8 billion. All told, the S&P 500 rose 44.98 points to 7,818.93. The Dow Jones Industrial Average added 253.38 to 51,521.28, and the Nasdaq composite climbed 122.48 to 27,599.79. Bond yields offered some slack on Tuesday after falling back from their highest levels in years or even decades. The yield on the 10-year Treasury, which is the focal point of the U.S. bond market, eased to 5.28 per cent from 5.31 per cent late Monday. It fell after oil prices steadied themselves somewhat. The price for a barrel of Brent crude oil, the international standard, dropped to roughly US$97 in the morning before pulling back to settle at US$100.58. While that was up 0.3 per cent from Monday’s settlement price, it’s still below the nearly US$110 it was at a few weeks ago. In stock markets abroad, indexes ticked higher in Europe as yields continue to swing in their bond markets amid concerns about high government debts and tight budgets. In France, tens of thousands of demonstrators marched in support of protests by students demanding more funding for schools. In Asia, Japan’s Nikkei 225 jumped 1.1 per cent, and Hong Kong’s Hang Seng climbed 1 per cent, but South Korea’s Kospi dropped 0.9 per cent. ___ Stan Choe, The Associated Press AP Business Writers Chan Ho-him and Matt Ott contributed to this report.

item.title: Emera bulks up for power demand boom with $14.3B Canadian Utilities deal
item.description: Canadian utility companies Emera and Canadian Utilities said on Tuesday they would merge to create a combined company with an enterprise value of about $72 billion (US$50.46 billion).
item.dc:creator: Reuters Staff
item.content:encoded: Emera said on Tuesday it would buy peer Canadian Utilities for $14.3 billion in stock, strengthening its financial muscle as power companies ramp up investments to tap into booming demand. The deal, which will create one of Canada’s top power providers with an enterprise value of about $72 billion, comes when utilities across North America move ahead with costly upgrades of aging grid and transmission infrastructure. “As demand rises from electrification trends and major infrastructure development, the combined company will be better positioned to help meet growing energy needs,” Emera CEO Scott Balfour, who will lead the combined company, said in a statement. U.S. power firms NextEra Energy and Dominion Energy in May agreed to merge in a $66.8 billion deal amid soaring electricity demand fueled by the rapid expansion of data centers supporting the adoption of AI. Emera said the deal would support a planned $32 billion capital program through 2030, with an expected annual rate-base growth of seven to eight per cent. The combined company will have about six million customers and a presence in high-growth markets through a portfolio of 12 regulated utilities. “Florida and Alberta will become the company’s two largest jurisdictions, representing approximately 45 per cent and 34 per cent respectively,” Balfour said in a conference call. Deal closing in 2027 Under the offer, Class A shareholders of Canadian Utilities, excluding ATCO, will receive 0.755 Emera shares and Class B shareholders will get 0.819 for each share held. The deal values Canadian Utilities’ Class A shares at about $51.57 each, a premium of roughly 0.7 per cent to the stock’s close on Monday, according to LSEG data. Meanwhile, ATCO, which holds nearly 37 per cent of the outstanding non-voting shares and all outstanding voting shares of Canadian Utilities, will separate into a publicly traded industrial services company. Emera shares were down 1.2 per cent, Canadian Utilities rose 1.4 per cent and ATCO jumped 12.8 per cent in morning trading. The deal is expected to close in the third or fourth quarter of 2027 and add to earnings per share in the first full year following the completion. The new company will operate as Emera and maintain its public company headquarters in Halifax. --- Reporting by Katha Kalia in Bengaluru; Editing by Jonathan Ananda and Sriraj Kalluvila

item.title: Nortera, B&G Foods drop merger attempt after competition watchdog steps in
item.description: Food giants Nortera and B&G Foods Canada are abandoning their proposed deal after the Competition Bureau sought to block the move.
item.dc:creator: The Canadian Press
item.content:encoded: Food giants Nortera and B&G Foods Canada are abandoning their proposed deal after the Competition Bureau sought to block the move. The two companies say Quebec-based Nortera has halted its bid to buy the Green Giant and Le Sieur brands of canned and frozen vegetables in Canada from New Jersey-based B&G Foods. A Competition Bureau investigation in August found that the acquisition would likely harm competition through higher prices and fewer choices in the wholesale supply of those vegetables, which include freezer staples such as corn and peas. Interim competition commissioner Jeanne Pratt has noted that Nortera is already Canada’s dominant processor of many canned and frozen veggies, which it sells under the Del Monte and Arctic Gardens brands. It has also been the exclusive producer of Green Giant and Le Sieur in Canada for 30 years, announcing in October 2025 a deal to buy the brands outright from B&G. The two companies say B&G Foods will continue to own and operate Green Giant Canada and Nortera will remain its main co-manufacturer. --- This report by The Canadian Press was first published Oct. 6, 2026.

item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米国株式市場＝Ｓ＆Ｐ５００とナスダックが最高値更新、原油価格の安定で 5:14 配信

2026年9月28日に撮影 REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration

［ニューヨーク　６日　ロイター］ - 米国株式市場は続伸。幅広い銘柄が買われ、Ｓ＆Ｐ総合５００種とナスダック総合が最高値を更新して引けた。原油価格が落ち着き、米国債利回りも低下したことで、ここ数週間に投資家を悩ませてきた懸念が和らぎ、市場の関心は間近に迫った第３・四半期決算発表シーズンに向かった。

ダウ工業株３０種は８月５日に付けた終値での最高値を５％余り下回っている。

ウェルスパイア・アドバイザーズのシニアバイスプレジデント、オリバー・パーシェ氏は、原油価格が安定または下落すると「エネルギー価格高騰によるインフレへの不安が和らぐため利回りが低下し、それが株価の上昇を後押しする」と指摘。「ここ数週間の市場はこうした構図で動いてきた」と述べた。

超大型株「マグニフィセント・セブン」のうち６銘柄が上昇し、相場を押し上げた。一方、小型株指数のラッセル２０００はアンダーパフォームした。

人工知能（ＡＩ）関連株への買いは依然として健在で、フィラデルフィア半導体株指数（ＳＯＸ指数）も上昇した。ＡＩ関連インフラへの支出は貿易統計にも表れ、８月の資本財輸入は４．４％増加した。

Ｓ＆Ｐ５００の主要１１業種では、ヘルスケアを除く全業種が上昇。公益事業が上昇率トップだった。

第３・四半期決算シーズンは来週始まり、１３日には複数の大手金融機関が発表を予定している。

個別銘柄では半導体設計のマーベル・テクノロジーが５．８％上昇。データセンター向け半導体の旺盛な需要を背景に、２０２８年の売上高見通しを引き上げたことを好感した。

半導体大手ＡＭＤも２．８％高。リサ・スー最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）が、急増するＡＩ需要に対応するため２７年に半導体供給を大幅に増やす計画を示した。

電力大手コンステレーション・エナジーは１２．３％急伸。アルファベット傘下のグーグルと３５９０メガワットの電力供給契約を結んだことが材料視された。

ニューヨーク証券取引所では値上がり銘柄数が値下がり銘柄数を１．９３対１の比率で上回った。ナスダックでも１．０１対１で値上がり銘柄が多かった。

米取引所の合算出来高は１６５億株。直近２０営業日の平均は１７５億１０００万株。

item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
原油先物ほぼ横ばい、中東供給増とフーシ派攻撃巡る懸念見極め 5:11 配信

ホルムズ海峡を航行する船舶。オマーン・ムサンダムから２日撮影。REUTERS/Stringer

Scott DiSavino

[ニューヨーク　６日　ロイター] - 米国時間の原油先物は序盤の下げを取り戻し、ほぼ横ばいで終了した。中東からの原油輸出の増加や主要７カ国（Ｇ７）による緊急備蓄からのディーゼル燃料放出計画と、イエメンの親イラン武装組織フーシ派の攻撃に伴う供給懸念とを見極める展開となった。

清算値は、北海ブレント先物が０．２６ドル（０．３％）高の１バレル＝１００．５８ドル。米ＷＴＩ先物は０．０１ドル高の８９．４４ドル。

大手石油商社ビトルの最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は６日、価格上昇圧力を和らげるために必要な量とされる日量約１２００万バレルの原油と同２００万バレルの石油製品が、過去７─１０日間に中東から出荷されたと明らかにした。

サウジアラビアのアブドルアジズエネルギー相も６日、紅海沿岸の石油輸出拠点ヤンブーに通じる東西パイプラインの送油量が、同日朝の時点で５８０万バレルに達したと明らかにした。

こうした中、サウジアラビア航空当局は、フーシ派との対立が激化する中、ジャザンとナジュランにあるサウジの２空港が５日に攻撃の標的となり、３人が負傷し、限定的な被害が出たと明らかにした。中東でのさらなる供給途絶の可能性が意識され、原油価格の下落幅は限定的なものにとどまった。

item.title: ＮＹ外為市場＝ユーロ上昇、仏債利回り低下が追い風
item.description: ［ニューヨーク ６日 ロイター］ - ニューヨーク外為市場ではユーロが上昇し、１日としては７週間ぶりの大幅な上昇を記録す...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ＮＹ外為市場＝ユーロ上昇、仏債利回り低下が追い風 5:05 配信

2026年3月撮影。REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustrationト

［ニューヨーク　６日　ロイター］ - ニューヨーク外為市場ではユーロが上昇し、１日としては７週間ぶりの大幅な上昇を記録する見通し。フランス国債利回りの低下を受け、ユーロ圏債市場の緊張に対する懸念が和らいだ。

ユーロ／ドルは０．３５％高の１．１２６ドル。１日としては８月１９日以来の大幅高となる見通し。前日の取引では、約１年５カ月ぶりの安値を付ける場面もあった。

主要通貨に対するドル指数は０．３２％安の１０１．８３。１日の下げとしては９月３日以来最大となる見込み。

原油相場の落ち着きを背景に、仏１０年債利回りは６日の取引で低下。同債利回りはここ数週間で急上昇し、指標となる独債との利回り格差は月初に２０１１年のユーロ圏債務危機以来の最大水準に拡大していた。

ポンド／ドルは１週間ぶりの高値となる１．３２８３ドルを付けた後、終盤の取引では０．４２％高の１．３２７５ドル。ポンドも１日としては８月１９日以来の大幅高となる勢い。    　一方、ドル／円は０．１１％高の１５８．０８円。    　日銀の植田和男総裁は６日、基調的な物価上昇率が２％に近づいている中、金融環境が緩和的なことを踏まえれば「経済・物価・金融情勢に応じて、引き続き政策金利を引き上げ、金融緩和度合いを調整していくことになる」と述べた。その上で、政策調整のタイミングやペースは、経済・物価の中心的な見通しが実現する確度やリスクを点検しながら検討していくとした。    　米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）は月末の会合で金利を据え置くと見込まれている。ＣＭＥのフェドウォッチによると、同会合で０．２５％ポイント利上げが実施される確率は約１９％と、１週間前の約５１％から低下した。しかし、市場が織り込む１２月の米連邦公開市場委員会（ＦＯＭＣ）での利上げ確率は８６％となっている。    　ゴールドマン・サックスのアナリストはレポートで、９月のドルの上昇について、米株式市場でのハイテクおよび人工知能（ＡＩ）関連銘柄の比重の高まりと、最近の米経済成長の好調さが一因だと指摘。ただ、ＦＲＢが金融引き締めに忍耐強いアプローチを強調していることなどを理由に、短期的なドルの強さについては慎重な見方を示した。    　こうした中、カンザスシティー地区連銀のシュミッド総裁は６日、長期金利の上昇が一部の経済活動の重しになっているとしても、ＦＲＢがインフレ抑制のために追加利上げを実施する必要があるとの考えを示した。

item.description: [６日 ロイター] - トランプ米大統領は６日、米ドルは「極めて強い」とし、強いドルは米経済が好調なことを示して...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
強いドルは米経済好調の証し、インフレもたらさず＝トランプ氏 4:32 配信

９月３０日撮影　REUTERS/Kevin Lamarque

[６日 ロイター] - トランプ米大統領は６日、米ドルは「極めて強い」とし、強いドルは米経済が好調なことを示していると述べた。

トランプ氏は記者団に対し「ドルは極めて強い。それは米国が好調だからだ」と発言。「強いドルには多くの利点がある。場合によっては（経済を）やや減速させるとの見方もできるが、強いドルは（経済に）活力をもたらす」と語った。

その上で「強いドルが何をもたらすか分かるか？インフレをもたらさないということだ」と述べた。

Oct 6 (Reuters) – President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Tuesday that the latest intelligence suggested Russia was preparing a “massive attack” on Ukraine.

“There is updated intelligence indicating that Russia is preparing a massive attack,” Zelenskiy said in his nightly video address.

“Ukrainian services and our air force are ready to respond to the extent permitted by our available means of defence.”

Show Full Article

Zelenskiy said Ukraine’s position depended largely on what its allies could provide in terms of weaponry to defend against a new Russian attack.

“A great deal depends on our partners, on every leader and every country in the world that has the defensive capabilities we need and can provide them to us,” he said.

“It is critically important that there be the political will to do so, particularly in the United States, in Europe and among our other partners.”

(Reporting by Ron Popeski and Oleksandr Kozhukhar; editing by Deepa Babington)

Police fire teargas as French school protests cause ‘heaviest toll in decades’

Reuters

06 October, 2026 11:00 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

(c) Copyright Thomson Reuters 2026

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

By Tilman Blasshofer, Cecile Mantovani and Lucien Libert STRASBOURG/LYON/PARIS, Oct 6 (Reuters) – Police fired tear gas at protesters outside French high schools on Tuesday as students, teachers and parents took to the streets on the biggest day of what Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu described as the most violent school protests in decades.

The protests, in which a teenager lost a hand on Monday, were the latest manifestation of public anger in a country where the far right and far left are surging ahead of a presidential election in the spring.

The government is under pressure to tame public debt amid weak growth, and has struggled with basic tasks such as passing a budget since President Emmanuel Macron’s allies lost their majority in a 2024 parliamentary vote.

Show Full Article

Lecornu told lawmakers at least 215 teenagers and 85 school staff had so far been injured in clashes, “the heaviest toll in decades paid by the school system”. His office said more than 700 police officers were also hurt.

Macron has convened Lecornu and other senior ministers at an emergency meeting on Tuesday, broadcaster BFM reported.

In Marseille and Nantes, protesters held up signs reading “The state has killed national education”. In Toulouse, parents linked arms at the front of a march through the city.

In Strasbourg, Lyon, Rennes and Paris, the demonstrations at times turned violent, with police firing tear gas and protesters lighting fires in the streets and hurling projectiles.

The Paris police said the clashes there had come about when some 300 people attempted to face off against security forces, adding that the protest was generally unfolding well elsewhere.

By late afternoon they said they were still clashing with a small contingent of people. Three storefronts had been damaged.

The protests began in September in the deprived suburbs of Paris, before spreading nationwide.

“There is such a gap between the elites and us,” said Hugo Vetzel, a recent high-school graduate in Strasbourg.

The High School Students Union said more than half of France’s high schools were blockaded or would close for the day. Some local education authorities have tried to move classes online.

Students complain about schools facing basic maintenance problems, from water leaks to rat infestations.

THOUSANDS OF ARRESTS

Rights groups, students and parent groups have accused authorities of using disproportionate force against minors. The government says the protest movement has been hijacked by outsiders and in some places deteriorated into urban violence.

France’s interior ministry said 6,100 people have been arrested since the protests began, the overwhelming majority of them minors. More than 1,800 people are being prosecuted for unspecified crimes, including 1,483 minors, the justice ministry said.

A teenager’s hand was blown off as high-school protesters clashed with riot police in northern France on Monday. The regional newspaper La Voix du Nord said the 15-year-old lost his hand and part of his lower arm after picking up a police grenade intended to be non-lethal.

“They want to divide the young people into good and bad protesters,” said Omar Slaouti, a high-school teacher in Argenteuil, a northwestern suburb of Paris. “If there were no trash cans on fire, the government would not have stepped back and become aware of the issues at stake.”

Six months before an election to replace Macron, his government and far-right leader Marine Le Pen’s National Rally party have accused hard-left France Unbowed (LFI) lawmakers and mayors of stoking the unrest. LFI denies the accusation.

“All the young people are in the streets. Everywhere there aren’t police, everything is going smoothly,” said Jean-Luc Melenchon, LFI’s presidential candidate.

PRIME MINISTER PROMISES A RESPONSE

Lecornu has ordered his ministers to tackle the students’ leading demands. Those include ensuring absent teachers are replaced, reviewing the length of the 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. school day and the need for longer lunch breaks.

The government will also look at repairs needed to ageing school buildings, said Lecornu, who demanded ministers send in their first proposals by the end of October.

Parent Emilie Lhomme said at a protest outside the Helene Boucher school in Paris that the government’s words were not enough: “That’s all fine and dandy, but that’s not what’s going to change the daily lives of our children,” she said.

Finding spare cash to implement educational reforms will be difficult.

The government is under pressure to try to narrow a ballooning budget deficit as investor concerns about France’s growing debt, weak growth and reluctance to rein in spending push the cost of borrowing higher. The yield on France’s 10-year bonds briefly hit a 24-year high of over 5% last week.

The surge in French borrowing costs has started to spill into the broader euro area, with the sliding euro currency the latest alarm bell for policy makers. Finance Minister Roland Lescure said on Tuesday there was no need for the European Central Bank to step in.

Le Pen, the far-right euro-sceptic populist leading the presidential race ahead of next spring’s election, set out plans to slash public spending if elected, seeking to establish her fiscal credibility as the bond market crisis deepens.

French spending on education has lagged inflation and the country’s students are trailing their OECD peers in overall performance, data from the PISA 2025 assessment shows.

(Reporting by Tilman Blasshofer in Strasbourg, Cecile Mantovani in Lyon, Lucien Libert, Juliette Jabkhiro, Elizabeth Pineau and Dominique Vidalon in Paris, Layli Foroudi in Argenteuil, Inti Landauro and Sudip Kar-Gupta in Brussels, and Dimitri Rhodes in Gdansk; Writing by Richard Lough and Makini Brice; Editing by Andrew Heavens and Peter Graff)

item.title: Shoppers to spend less this holiday season, willing to pay more for Canadian goods: PwC
item.description: TORONTO — A new report suggests Canadians plan to spend less this holiday season compared with last year, but more than half are willing to pay more for Canadian-made products over imported options.
item.dc:creator: The Canadian Press
item.content:encoded: TORONTO — A new report suggests Canadians plan to spend less this holiday season compared with last year, but more than half are willing to pay more for Canadian-made products over imported options. The report by PwC Canada says 54 per cent of those surveyed say they would choose a more expensive Canadian-made product over a similar imported option, up from 49 per cent last year. The shift comes as the firm’s holiday outlook report says Canadians plan to spend an average of $1,487 this holiday season, down 11 per cent from last year. PwC added that its survey was conducted in July and early August, before the recent escalation in the trade fight with the United States, so the findings may under-represent current Canadian sentiment. Adam Boutros, partner and national consumer markets leader at PwC Canada, says more Canadians than ever want their money to stay in Canada. The report was based on an online survey of 1,016 respondents between July 30 and Aug. 6. The Canadian Research Insights Council, an industry organization that promotes polling standards, says online surveys cannot be assigned a margin of error because they do not randomly sample the population. --- This report by The Canadian Press was first published Oct. 6, 2026.

item.title: Los países de América Latina con más pasajeros aéreos por habitante en 2026
item.description: Panamá lidera el listado regional con 4,59 pasajeros por habitante, seguido por Colombia y Chile. El indicador muestra una amplia brecha entre los mercados latinoamericanos y refleja el potencial de c ...
item.dc:creator: Carlos Cuevas
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg Línea — Latinoamérica y el Caribe aportan el 8,1% de los pasajeros del tráfico aéreo mundial, de acuerdo con las cifras más recientes de la oficina regional del Consejo Internacional de Aeropuertos (ACI-LAC). Sin embargo, el número de viajeros podría aumentar si hubiera una mayor desregulación y liberalización de los mercados. El potencial de la región para crecer recae, en cierta medida, “en el volumen de su población”, aunque lastimosamente el sector de la aviación no ha podido estimular el aumento de pasajeros per cápita, explicó recientemente el director general de ACI-LAC, Rafael Echevarne, a Bloomberg Línea. Brasil tiene una población aproximada de 214,2 millones de habitantes, pero registra apenas 1,1 pasajeros por habitante. En contraste, España, con alrededor de 49,8 millones de habitantes, registra 6,5 pasajeros por habitante, la cifra más alta a nivel internacional, según los datos de ACI-LAC. Este indicador no significa necesariamente que cada habitante haya viajado una determinada cantidad de veces. Se trata de la relación entre el número total de pasajeros y la población, por lo que también puede incluir viajeros internacionales, turistas y pasajeros en conexión. Ver más: Dos aeropuertos de Venezuela podrían atraer inversión privada, pero falta seguridad jurídica: ACI-LAC La comparación entre Brasil y España evidencia la brecha en el número de pasajeros por habitante, aunque las diferencias entre ambos mercados también responden a factores como el nivel de ingresos, el turismo y la conectividad. Un aumento de la conectividad y del número de pasajeros, tanto en rutas domésticas como internacionales, elevaría este indicador. “Obviamente, el perfil socioeconómico de los países cuenta mucho, ¿no? Cuando la renta per cápita es más alta, más puedes volar. Pero, realmente, vemos que hay una gran diferencia y creemos que hay un potencial para subir estos números”, aclaró Echevarne. Para el experto, la clave está en eliminar “barreras artificiales regulatorias” y “estimular la competencia entre aerolíneas”. Una mayor competencia, señaló, puede traducirse en precios más bajos de los tiquetes aéreos. Echevarne destacó que el mercado europeo permite a las aerolíneas operar entre los países de la Unión Europea bajo un marco mucho más integrado, mientras que en Latinoamérica persisten restricciones y acuerdos que pueden dificultar la expansión de una misma aerolínea entre distintos mercados. En Latinoamérica, a diferencia de otras regiones, existen accidentes geográficos importantes que también pueden convertirse en una oportunidad para el transporte aéreo. Colombia es un ejemplo, según Echevarne. “Colombia ha demostrado que depende del transporte aéreo para su desarrollo, tanto social como económico, debido a la geografía del país. Entonces es uno de aquellos países impulsores del crecimiento del transporte aéreo”, expuso. Panamá registra el mayor número de pasajeros por habitante de América Latina, con 4,59. Sin embargo, la cifra está distorsionada por el alto número de viajeros en tránsito que pasan por el Aeropuerto Internacional de Tocumen. “Eso está reflejando la particularidad de que Panamá es un hub de Copa Airlines”, comentó Echevarne. Colombia ocupa el segundo lugar, con 1,87 pasajeros por habitante, mientras que Chile se ubica tercero, con 1,84. El Aeropuerto Internacional El Dorado, en Bogotá, es además el segundo más transitado de la región. El panorama cambia cuando se analiza exclusivamente el número de pasajeros internacionales por habitante. En este caso, dos países centroamericanos lideran el listado: República Dominicana y Costa Rica. “No es una sorpresa que lideren porque son grandes destinos turísticos internacionales, por eso la cifra es tan alta”, ahondó Echevarne. “Pero, de nuevo, aquí vamos donde estábamos: es realmente revelador el gran potencial que Brasil tiene en la generación de más pasajeros, sobre todo internacionales”. Ver más: ¿Se puede descarbonizar la aviación sin encarecer los tiquetes? El reto pendiente de Latinoamérica

item.title: Allemagne-Un ancien directeur du renseignement arrêté pour des soupçons de trahison
item.description: L'ancien chef du service allemand du renseignement extérieur (BND), August Hanning, a été arrêté mardi pour des soupçons de tentative de trahison, une affaire qui constitue l'un des plus importants scandales ayant éclaboussé les services des renseignements allemands depuis la Guerre froide.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: L'ancien chef du service allemand du renseignement extérieur (BND), August Hanning, a été arrêté mardi pour des soupçons de tentative de trahison, une affaire qui constitue l'un des plus importants scandales ayant éclaboussé les services des renseignements allemands depuis la Guerre froide. August Hanning est accusé par le parquet d'avoir payé pour se procurer des documents secrets après avoir quitté ses fonctions et d'avoir utilisé ces documents pour effectuer une analyse au bénéfice d'un service étranger du renseignement. Les procureurs n'ont pas précisé dans l'immédiat de quel service étranger il s'agissait ni si l'analyse en question a effectivement été transmise à son destinataire voulu. D'après le magazine d'information Der Spiegel, les enquêteurs étudient un possible lien avec l'Azerbaïdjan, alors qu'August Hanning aurait été en contact avec un agent de ce pays. Le parquet fédéral a décliné une demande de commentaire, de même que la chancellerie. Aucun commentaire n'a pu être obtenu auprès d'August Hanning. Jamais, auparavant, un ex-chef du service du renseignement extérieur n'avait été arrêté en Allemagne, dont les relations en matière de renseignements avec des pays alliés pourraient pâtir de cette affaire, a déclaré un élu sécuritaire de haut rang. Dans un communiqué, le parquet a déclaré qu'August Hanning était "fortement suspecté d'espionnage perfide, d'avoir obtenu des secrets d'Etat, de tentative de trahison et d'espionnage". Selon les procureurs, August Hanning était convenu avec le responsable de bureau du BND, cinq ans après son départ du service, dont il a occupé la présidence pendant sept ans jusqu'en 2005, de recevoir des renseignements confidentiels en échange de paiements. Ce responsable de bureau, identifié comme étant Manfred D., dans le respect des règles de confidentialité en Allemagne, a également été arrêté mardi. Les deux hommes devaient comparaître devant un juge de la Cour fédérale de justice. L'AFFAIRE NE CONCERNERAIT PAS LA RUSSIE Manfred D. a été responsable de bureau du BND pour plusieurs présidents successifs du service, jusqu'en mars dernier, ce qui lui a potentiellement permis d'accéder à certains renseignements toujours d'actualité au moment où, d'après les procureurs, des documents ont été "siphonnés" du BND. Quelque 2.000 documents auraient été fournis par Manfred D. au fil des années, ont dit les procureurs, ajoutant que parmi ces documents figuraient des éléments classifiés destinés uniquement à un usage interne au BND et à des compte-rendus auprès de représentants de haut rang à la chancellerie. Selon le journal Sueddeutsche Zeitung, les documents en question concernent le programme nucléaire iranien et l'armée russe, de même que des documents classés secrets transmis par des services de renseignement alliés à propos d'autres pays. Les procureurs accusent August Hanning d'avoir utilisé des informations classifiées transmises par Manfred D. pour préparer une analyse destinée à un officier d'un service étranger du renseignement et d'avoir pendant des années partagé des informations politiques avec un représentant de ce service. Cette affaire ne concerne pas la Russie, selon une information obtenue par le Sueddeutsche Zeitung. L'actuel président du BND a déclaré que le service a lancé une enquête interne approfondie dès que les premiers soupçons sont apparus. "Il ne peut y avoir aucun compromis sur la sécurité interne", a ajouté Martin Jäger.

item.title: Kotak, IndusInd, Axis Bank shares jump on strong Q2 business updates
item.description: Lenders report strong credit and deposit growth aided by FCNR(B) inflows, though analysts flag concerns over CASA momentum ...
item.dc:creator: Subrata Panda
item.content:encoded: Shares of Kotak Mahindra Bank, IndusInd Bank and Axis Bank rose sharply on Tuesday after the lenders reported robust growth in advances and deposits in their quarterly business updates. This growth was aided by healthy mobilisation of FCNR(B) deposits. Kotak Mahindra Bank’s shares jumped 3.59 per cent to close at ₹431.25 on the BSE, while IndusInd Bank gained 2.79 per cent to end at ₹906.95. Axis Bank’s shares rose 2.01 per cent to ₹1,248.50. However, RBL Bank’s shares closed 0.72 per cent lower at ₹414 on the BSE compared with the previous day’s close. On Monday, Kotak Mahindra Bank reported robust net advances (period-end) growth of 25 per cent year-on-year (Y-o-Y) and 13 per cent quarter-on-quarter (Q-o-Q). Excluding advances linked to FCNR(B) deposits, loan growth remained firm at around 21 per cent Y-o-Y and 10 per cent Q-o-Q. Deposits grew 23 per cent Y-o-Y and 14 per cent Q-o-Q, aided by FCNR(B) inflows. Excluding these, deposit growth was more measured at 13 per cent Y-o-Y and 4 per cent Q-o-Q. Current account savings account (CASA) balances grew 11 per cent Y-o-Y and 8 per cent Q-o-Q. The bank mobilised $5.78 billion through FCNR(B) deposits during the quarter. Axis Bank, India’s third-largest private sector lender, said its deposits grew 5.8 per cent sequentially and 20.7 per cent Y-o-Y to ₹14.52 trillion as of September 30, while gross advances rose 8.8 per cent Q-o-Q and 22.7 per cent YoY to ₹13.85 trillion. The lender mobilised $10.62 billion (₹1.02 trillion) in FCNR(B) deposits under the Reserve Bank of India’s swap facility introduced earlier this year.   “While the outcome is good on the loan growth front, the question is sustainability plus core deposit growth around 12-13 per cent for Kotak (Mahindra Bank) and Axis (Bank) isn’t that great. That goes to show that eventually loan growth will have to come down from current levels. CASA growth is also 10 to 11 per cent similar to HDFC Bank showing the pressure that exists in CASA across the system. CASA ratios continue to decline even on core deposit growth basis”, said Suresh Ganapathy, MD&Head - Financial Services Research, Macquarie Capital.  Meanwhile, IndusInd Bank’s net advances grew 11.2 per cent Y-o-Y to ₹3.62 trillion as of September 30, 2026, outpacing the 10.1 per cent growth in deposits to ₹4.29 trillion. IndusInd Bank’s CASA ratio declined to 28 per cent from 30.7 per cent a year earlier and 29.4 per cent in June. The lender mobilised $3.51 billion in FCNR(B) deposits under the RBI’s deposit swap facility, with outstanding loans of about ₹16,564 crore extended from its GIFT City branch against these deposits as of September-end. And, RBL Bank’s total deposits rose 34 per cent Y-o-Y to around ₹1.56 trillion in the quarter ended September 30 (Q2FY27), while gross advances grew 40 per cent to around ₹1.43 trillion. (Disclosure: Entities controlled by the Kotak family have a significant holding in Business Standard Pvt Ltd)

item.title: Why have India-US trade talks stalled again and what's next?
item.description: Senior officials in India and the United States have indicated long-running efforts to finalise a bilateral trade agreement have stalled, again.
item.dc:creator: Shivangi Acharya, Manoj Kumar
item.content:encoded: Senior officials in India and the United States have indicated long-running efforts to finalise a bilateral trade agreement have stalled, again. Both nations had agreed to a [USN:L1N3YY0U1 TEXT:"framework for the deal"] in February which brought down to 18% [USN:L1N3UJ03Y TEXT:"from 50%"] the punitive tariff on most Indian goods imposed in August last year after a previous round of [USN:L4N3TT0LO TEXT:"talks collapsed"]. In the meantime, the Supreme Court invalidated US President Donald Trump's use of emergency powers to impose sweeping tariffs globally, leading to a 10% [USN:L1N3ZG0T5 TEXT:"baseline rate"]. But a final deal between two of the world's biggest economies remains elusive. WHY HAVE TRADE TALKS HIT A WALL? Trade talks have [USN:L1N45R03N TEXT:"reached a "plateau""] with little room for manoeuvre, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said earlier this week, following United States Trade Representative Jamieson Greer's comment that a deal is [USN:S0N40K049 TEXT:"not "imminent"]." Neither side has detailed reasons for the delay in finalising the deal. But talks in the past months have met with complications, most recently [USN:L1N4590XN TEXT:"a new US law"] that paves the way for up to 100% tariffs on Indian goods because of New Delhi's purchase of Russian oil. Those purchases have not been significantly reduced. The potentially stiff levy goes against New Delhi's [USN:L4N42U08S TEXT:"efforts to secure"] tariff terms better than peer economies, including Vietnam and China. A deal has also been held back because Washington is [USN:L1N4290B6 TEXT:"yet to complete"] a Section 301 trade investigation on several nations over alleged excess industrial capacity. The probe is to evaluate whether such overproduction is hurting or undercutting American industries. Unless this probe is completed, it is hard to tell what final tariff Indian goods will attract. Overall, bilateral ties between India and the US have been rocky this past year, casting a shadow on [USN:L1N45904J TEXT:"efforts to stabilise"] their trade partnership. Events including a [USN:L1N42K089 TEXT:"US military attack"] on a ship off Oman that killed three Indian seafarers and [USN:L1N3TP08X TEXT:"India rejecting"] Trump's repeated claim of brokering a ceasefire with Pakistan have hurt relations. WHAT IS AT STAKE? The US is India's largest export market and exports have so far been [USN:L4N3XL16E TEXT:"resilient"]. India's goods exports to the United States rose to $42.79 billion in April-August from $40.39 billion a year earlier. In the fiscal year 2025/26, India enjoyed a nearly $34 billion trade surplus with the US. India says many of its largest export categories to the US, including generic pharmaceuticals and smartphones, are not subject to the current 10% levy. But analysts say that in the absence of a trade deal, India risks higher US tariffs from the ongoing trade probe and purchase of Russian oil, even if it could negotiate for waivers under the sanctions law. Another increase in tariffs could hurt businesses, dent market sentiment and hurt the Indian currency, which is already trading close to record lows. WHAT MORE DO THE TWO SIDES WANT? India is striving to protect politically sensitive sectors, particularly agriculture, while securing [USN:L1N43F08Q TEXT:"better tariff treatment"] for its exporters. India has sought to keep dairy, poultry, rice, wheat and other farm products outside the scope of market-opening commitments. It wants greater certainty over US tariffs before making concessions. The Trump administration wants India to cut Russian oil purchases, arguing Indian purchases of Russian crude help finance the war in Ukraine. India says decisions on where to source fuel are driven by [USN:L4N45A0SX TEXT:"the energy needs"] of its 1.4-billion-strong population. Russian crude became particularly important after Moscow's full-scale invasion of Ukraine because it was available at discounted prices. The war in the Middle East and resulting disruptions have sharpened the calculation over energy imports. ARE FURTHER TALKS PLANNED? US Secretary of State Marco Rubio is expected to visit India later this month, when two-way talks could make some progress. Modi and Trump, who spoke by phone on September 30, are also expected to speak again soon to review progress. Modi is expected to visit the US in December for a G20 leaders' meet.

item.title: Planned Moldova-Romania power line to be named after Trump
item.description: A planned high-voltage power line linking Romania and Moldova will be named the "Trump Liberty Line," the US embassy in Chisinau said on Monday, making it the latest infrastructure project to bear the name of US President Donald Trump.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A planned high-voltage power line linking Romania and Moldova will be named the "Trump Liberty Line," the US embassy in Chisinau said on Monday, making it the latest infrastructure project to bear the name of US President Donald Trump. The embassy said in a post on X that the project, "backed by a $130 million US government investment", would strengthen Moldova's energy security and independence "The Government of the Republic of Moldova supports initiatives that benefit the citizens of the Republic of Moldova, especially those that ensure the country's security and energy infrastructure," government spokesperson Dumitru Ciorici told Reuters "The Romanian government has always supported interconnecting projects between Romania and Moldova, and the fact the United States supports and finances them only reconfirms their strategic importance," said government spokeswoman Ioana Dogioiu. Moldova, one of Europe's poorest countries and a candidate for European Union membership, imports most of its electricity via existing links with Romania and Ukraine. Russian attacks on Ukraine's power infrastructure have disrupted those supplies in the past Trump's name has been attached to a growing number of projects around the world, including a proposed transport corridor through Armenia and a planned military base in Poland, as governments seek to win favour with the US president

item.title: For Trump’s Treasury, the sting is in the auction ‘tail’
item.description: US Treasury auctions are supposed to be dull, predictable, and non-newsworthy affairs. But these are not normal times, and the Trump administration now risks seeing weak debt sales make headline news.
item.dc:creator: Jamie McGeever
item.content:encoded: US Treasury auctions are supposed to be dull, predictable, and non-newsworthy affairs. But these are not normal times, and the Trump administration now risks seeing weak debt sales make headline news. The Treasury plans to sell nearly $120 billion of debt this week, the first sales outside of T-bills in two weeks: $58 billion of three-year notes on Tuesday, $39 billion of 10-year notes on Wednesday, and $22 billion of 30-year bonds on Thursday. These might normally be non-events, but they're under increasing scrutiny because the September 22-24 auctions were remarkably weak, particularly the five-year note auction on Sept. 23, which helped spark the biggest rise in bond yields since April last year. Yields have not come down since and have instead powered ahead to multi-decade highs across most maturities. It's worth stating that there's next to zero chance that the US would ever have a "failed" debt auction. Primary dealers – the 26 Wall Street banks and institutions currently approved by the New York Fed as Treasury market makers – will always participate. They effectively underwrite the sales, ensuring the $30 trillion US debt market – the most liquid market in the world – functions smoothly. This, in turn, keeps the entire global financial system chugging along, as well. Trillions of dollars of global debt, assets, and market derivatives use Treasuries as a reference. US government bonds are also the collateral used to lubricate the pipes of US and global financial plumbing - repo agreements, interbank lending, and funding. In short, as long as US debt is the lynchpin of the global financial system, there will always be buyers at Treasury auctions. The issue, as ever, is the price at which these sales clear. Right now, borrowing costs on the secondary market are the highest since the mid to early 2000s, so it is reasonable to assume that Treasury will pay comparably high rates on the primary market. But as the most recent auctions have shown, there is also still room for negative surprises. TOO BIG TO TAIL? The $70 billion sale of five-year notes on September 23 was one of the most alarming in recent memory. Demand as measured by the 'bid-to-cover' ratio was the lowest in nine years. Treasury ultimately sold the notes at 5.033%, which was more than three basis points above the market yield at the bidding deadline. Three basis points might not sound like a lot, but for a five-year auction, that’s extraordinary. It was the largest so-called "tail" since June 2022. To find the last time a five-year auction had a 3 bps "tail," JP Morgan analysts note, you have to go all the way back to 2011, when a brewing debt ceiling crisis would lead to a credit rating downgrade that August. Moving back to the present, concerns about the dire US fiscal outlook have pushed up long-term borrowing costs. As a result, the Trump administration is widely expected to gradually shift the weight of the Treasury’s huge borrowing requirements towards the shorter - and cheaper - end of the curve. This is why the five-year auction two weeks ago caused such alarm. "Tails" of 3 bps are common in longer bond auctions, but not in sales of debt that sit right in the so-called "belly" of the yield curve. If Treasury is being forced to pay higher premiums to shift these notes, then Houston, we have a problem. Fat auction “tails” can be a result of multiple forces, including market volatility on the day itself or more worrying fundamental issues that might erode demand over time. It's often difficult to untangle the two dynamics, as they are not mutually exclusive. On a more optimistic note, these jitters haven’t migrated to the front end of the curve. Yet. Three-year and 10-year yields are up around 50 basis points from their last auctions a month ago, hovering around 4.96% and 5.32%, respectively. The 30-year yield is up around 35 bps at 5.65%. That should be high enough to attract solid demand and ensure smooth sales, right? Probably. But if there’s a sting in the tails, volatility and uncertainty could bite across the market. Investors will be watching like, well, hawks. (The opinions expressed here are those of the author, a columnist for Reuters) Enjoying this column? US and China discuss reciprocal visits to nuclear sites: Reports

The idea of reciprocal visits was initially raised by China in meetings with US officials this year and visits to US Department of Energy national laboratories and equivalent Chinese facilities were discussed, CNN said, citing a source familiar with the matter.

US and Chinese flags displayed on a security barrier on the day of an official visit by Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife, Peng Liyuan, to the White House in Washington DC on Sep 25, 2026. (File Photo: Reuters/Evan Vucci)

FAST

The United States has discussed starting reciprocal visits to nuclear sites with China, and plans to continue pushing in meetings in the coming months, CNN reported on Tuesday (Oct 6), citing sources familiar with the matter.

The idea of reciprocal visits was initially raised by China in meetings with US officials this year and visits to US Department of Energy national laboratories and equivalent Chinese facilities were discussed, CNN said, citing a source.

The discussions between US and Chinese officials have mainly been on the sidelines of gatherings by the UN Security Council's five veto-wielding permanent members, CNN reported.

Reuters could not immediately verify the report. The White House and the Chinese embassy in Washington did not respond to requests for comment outside business hours.

US President Donald Trump called for trilateral arms control negotiations between the US, China and Russia when he met President Xi Jinping last month. However, the two leaders did not discuss the possibility of nuclear site visits during their talks, the CNN report said, citing a US official.

Beijing has said its nuclear arsenal is far smaller than those of Russia and the US, something it says makes its participation in such talks unnecessary.

Another meeting between Trump and Xi is widely considered likely this year, potentially at November's Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in China or during Group of 20 meetings in the US in December.

By the time the two leaders meet again, it is expected that further lower-level discussions on possible nuclear site visits will have taken place, CNN said.

item.description: STOCKHOLM: The Belgian-American Francis Halzen won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics for his work creating an Antarctic observatory of ice to detect high-energy neutrinos, elusive subatomic particles that can reveal otherwise inaccessible information about the cosmos.Halzen, 82, realised that pristine ice at th

Francis Halzen wins Nobel physics prize for Antarctic 'ghost particle' hunt

Eva Olsson, Ellen Moons, and Mark Pearce sit as they announce Francis Halzen as the recipient of the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics during a press conference at the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences in Stockholm, Sweden, Oct 6, 2026. (Photo: TT News Agency/Christine Olsson via REUTERS)

FAST

STOCKHOLM: The Belgian-American Francis Halzen won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics for his work creating an Antarctic observatory of ice to detect high-energy neutrinos, elusive subatomic particles that can reveal otherwise inaccessible information about the cosmos. Halzen, 82, realised that pristine ice at the South Pole could be used to track such neutrinos, sometimes known as "ghost particles" for the way they pass through the Earth without a trace, only interacting with matter extremely rarely. "The messengers bring information from the cosmos," Eva Olsson, of the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences, told a press conference. "They open the door to distant galaxies and tell us about the processes of exploding stars." HALZEN HAILED FOR DETECTING "MESSENGERS FROM THE COSMOS" The interactions registered by the IceCube observatory provide information about how high-energy neutrinos are created and may even reveal previously unknown phenomena, the Academy said.

In 2014, the US-based Smithsonian magazine dubbed Halzen "Neutrino Man" when giving him one of its Ingenuity Awards, acclaiming him for an "amazing experiment (that) heralds the beginning of a new era in astronomy". It even published a comic illustrating his life: "How One Physicist’s Pursuit of the Cosmos Took Off in Antarctica". The observatory - in effect a telescope that shows neutrinos instead of light - is set in a cubic kilometre of Antarctic ice, which extends to a depth of 2,500 metres below the surface near the Amundsen-Scott South Pole Station. More than 5,000 sensors await blips from the nearly massless high-energy neutrinos, which unlike other particles do not lose energy or change direction, in the hope of tracing their paths back to exploding stars, gamma-ray bursts, and cataclysmic phenomena involving black holes and neutron stars. They can expect to register about one per day. Halzen, a professor at the University of Wisconsin–Madison in the United States, first presented his idea in 1988 for capturing neutrino traces at the South Pole, but the project was not completed until 2011. "I have to emphasise how lucky I was because, when we started this project, everybody realised this was maybe a good idea, but very few thought it would work, including myself," Halzen told the press conference by telephone. Neutrinos are electrically neutral, undisturbed by any magnetic field, which means that, in contrast to electromagnetic waves such as visible light, the direction from which they arrive points directly back to their source.

Related:

Medicine Nobel goes to US-German trio for pioneering light-based control of cells

FRUITS OF HALZEN'S RESEARCH YET TO COME The observatory has determined that high-energy neutrinos originate within but also far outside our own Milky Way galaxy, setting in motion an interstellar quest to find the objects and processes that create them. Through the long winter at the South Pole, when bringing anything in or out is difficult as temperatures below minus 50°C (minus 58 Fahrenheit) preclude even aircraft landing, a skeleton crew of "winterovers" has to maintain the observatory. The station, home to many other activities, can house as many as 150 people and has an industrial kitchen, dining room, gym and even a greenhouse. Last week it celebrated the sun's return above the horizon after six months of night with a six-hole ice-golf tournament. An extension, IceCube-Gen2, encompassing 8 cubic kilometres of ice, is planned to become operational in 2033 and will be able to detect 10 times as many neutrinos, including much weaker ones. Halzen said the main fruits of his work were yet to be seen and that it was too early to say exactly what it could reveal about the universe. "The real excitement is that I cannot answer that question yet," he said. "This is just an introduction to the science, the astronomy is still to come." WINNERS FROM EINSTEIN TO BOHR AND THE CURIES Belgian Prime Minister Bart De Wever congratulated Halzen on the recognition of "a life dedicated to unraveling the greatest secrets of the cosmos through its most minuscule manifestations". The physics laureate receives an award of 12 million Swedish crowns (US$1.2 million). Past winners include several other neutrino research pioneers, for instance Japan's Takaaki Kajita and Arthur McDonald from Canada in 2015. The Nobel Prizes were established under the will of Swedish inventor and entrepreneur Alfred Nobel, whose fortune was built in part on the invention of dynamite. Physics was prominent in Nobel's will and the prize remains one of the discipline's highest distinctions. Over the decades, it has recognised discoveries that have fundamentally reshaped humanity's understanding of the universe. Among past laureates are some of the most celebrated figures in science, including Albert Einstein, Marie and Pierre Curie, Max Planck and Niels Bohr, whose work helped establish the foundations of modern physics. The prize is presented in Stockholm on Dec 10, the anniversary of Nobel's death.

Source: Reuters/fh

item.title: Barrick secures 15-year North Mara mining licences in Tanzania
item.description: The latest approval removes tenure risk, leaving Barrick to reverse a sharp first-half production decline.
item.dc:creator: Northern Miner Staff
item.content:encoded:
Barrick secures 15-year North Mara mining licences in Tanzania

Henry Lazenby | October 5, 2026 | 12:10 pm Top Companies   Africa   Canada   Gold

( Image by Twiga Partnership, Facebook. )

Tanzania has renewed Barrick Mining’s (TSX: ABX; NYSE: B) licences for the North Mara gold mine for 15 years, securing its operating tenure as the company weighs an expansion.

North Mara is a combined open-pit and underground operation about 540 km northwest of Dodoma and 20 km south of the Kenyan border. Barrick owns 84% and Tanzania holds the remaining 16%. The mine produced 249,000 attributable oz. last year.

“Relations at North Mara mine have strengthened since Barrick took over,” Tarime district commissioner Maj. Edward Gowele said in Barrick’s Monday release. “Residents now really view the mine as a community partner.”

North Mara’s two special mining licences were last renewed for 15 years in 2012. The latest approval removes that separate tenure risk, leaving Barrick to reverse a sharp first-half production decline, meet North Mara’s attributable 2026 guidance of 200,000 to 230,000 oz. and decide whether to expand the North Mara-Bulyanhulu complex.

Barrick’s Toronto-traded shares were down 1% at $56.84 (US$39.87) apiece by mid-Monday, after tracking 20% higher over the past 12 months. Bids have tested $42.62 and $74.00 over the same period.

Production test

Attributable output fell 47% to 68,000 oz. in the first half from 129,000 oz. a year earlier. All-in sustaining costs rose 79% to US$2,283 per oz. from US$1,272 per ounce. Barrick cited lower grades at North Mara among the factors raising company-wide second-quarter costs.

Barrick maintained North Mara’s guidance at 200,000 to 230,000 oz. and all-in sustaining costs of US$1,520-US$1,680 per oz. The mine must produce 132,000 to 162,000 oz. in the second half to reach that range.

North Mara output is expected to rise next year. Barrick is studying upgrades to remove processing bottlenecks and expand the North Mara-Bulyanhulu complex.

North Mara held attributable proven and probable reserves of 43 million tonnes grading 2.32 grams gold per tonne for 3.2 million oz. at the end of 2025, Barrick reported.

State reset

Barrick bought the 36% of Acacia Mining it didn’t already own in September 2019 and took direct control of North Mara. Under then-CEO Mark Bristow, it reached a settlement with Tanzania the following month and formalized it in January 2020, agreeing to pay $300 million, give the state a 16% free-carried interest in the mines and split their economic benefits equally.

The accord created Twiga Minerals to manage North Mara and Bulyanhulu. Since 2019, Barrick says its Tanzanian operations have contributed about $5.3 billion to the country, including $1.2 billion last year.

LBMA trial

The renewal comes as the London Bullion Market Association prepares for a six-week High Court trial beginning Wednesday over the deaths of two 23-year-old artisanal miners at North Mara in 2019. Their families allege Tanzanian police, private guards or both killed the men in separate incidents that July and December.

Barrick took operational control in September, between the incidents. It isn’t a defendant in the London case and declined to comment to Reuters , the news outlet reported Monday.

The claim alleges the LBMA negligently kept India-based refiner MMTC-PAMP that processed North Mara gold on its ‘good delivery list’ despite reports of abuses at the mine. The list determines which refiners’ bars are accepted in London’s wholesale bullion market.

The LBMA denies liability, saying it certifies refiners rather than mines and had no control over North Mara or Tanzanian police.

The association held about £1.4 million ($1.8 million) in reserves at the end of 2025 and could face £3 million in claimants’ legal costs before damages if it loses, Bloomberg reported on Monday.

A ruling holding the LBMA responsible could set a precedent for compensation over abuses at supplying mines and threaten its role in global gold trading, John Meyer, a mining analyst at SP Angel, said in a note on Monday. The court has stayed another 26 claims and five potential claims until after the trial, according to the LBMA.

News / GuruFocus / SpaceX Stock Jumps as Musk Adopts Trump 'Super Intelligence' Term

SpaceX Stock Jumps as Musk Adopts Trump 'Super Intelligence' Term Less than 1 min read

SPCX SpaceX stock is in focus Monday after CEO Elon Musk said the company plans to rename its artificial intelligence unit SpaceXAI to SpaceXSI, adopting a term favored by President Donald Trump. Shares of SpaceX SPCX were up more than 2% in early Monday trading, putting the stock in focus as investors weigh the significance of the proposed branding change. Musk confirmed the plan in response to an X user who asked whether SpaceXAI would be renamed. He did not provide a timetable or additional details about when the change would take effect. The proposed name follows Trump's recent push for U.S. agencies to use super intelligence and the abbreviation SI instead of artificial intelligence and AI. Trump made the case for the terminology during a speech to the United Nations General Assembly last month. SpaceX had not changed the SpaceXAI account on X at the time of the Reuters report. The company also had not provided a timeline for the rebranding.
